evaluator: Blind Stagebench Phase 1 evaluator: rebuilt the sealed artifact from source, served dist/ on a local port, and drove it under Playwright/Chromium with an AnalyserNode tapped in parallel off the node that feeds AudioDestinationNode, plus an injected fake Web MIDI device.
summary: An unusually disciplined Phase 1. Everything the phase contract asks for is present and independently verifiable in the running build: 73 keys E1-E7 (43W/30B, all inside the keybed), aspect 3.0951 against the variant's 3.0951, deck/keybed 0.5400/0.4600, width 0.9500 of 1440px, and all six section fractions exact to spec v1.2.0. Pointer, computer keyboard, focused-key Space/Enter and Web MIDI all reach one shared note lifecycle; sustain, all-notes-off, blur, MIDI disconnect and unmount all return the bus to digital silence. The honesty contract is exemplary: I drove all 146 panel controls in the live build and the master bus stayed at peak 0.00000, and an instrumented node census (2 sine + 1 triangle oscillator, 1 biquad, one 4320-frame 48kHz buffer, zero decodeAudioData, zero audio fetches) matches IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json line for line. The one real defect is gain staging: master gain is a fixed 0.7 with no headroom scaling or limiter, so the bus peaks at 1.121 on a two-note interval and 4.927 on sixteen notes - every chord hard-clips at the destination.

evidence: Single notes are dependable and piano-shaped across the keybed. Measured envelope of MIDI note 40 at velocity 100 (analyser peak, ms after note-on): 300ms 0.5653, 800ms 0.4488, 1500ms 0.3304, 3000ms 0.1567; note 84 over the same marks: 0.3846, 0.1426, 0.0395, 0.0030 - low notes ring far longer than high ones, as the pitch-scaled decay in src/audio/pianoVoice.ts:32-35 intends.

Release behaves: holding note 60 for 1200ms gave peak 0.21822, and 120ms after note-off it read 0.00237 (RELEASE_SECONDS 0.14, src/audio/pianoVoice.ts:65). Velocity behaves per note: pointer strike at the top of the key measured 0.16918 vs 0.88528 at the front lip; MIDI velocity 20 measured 0.05170 vs 0.59394 at velocity 100.

Level does not behave in sum. Tapping the gain node that feeds AudioDestinationNode, measured peaks for simultaneous MIDI notes at velocity 100 were 1 note 0.57581, 2 notes 1.12108, 4 notes 2.03609, 8 notes 2.81494, 16 notes 4.92725, and 40 notes 4.09918. Anything from a two-note interval upward exceeds 0 dBFS, so Chrome's destination hard-clips; the 16-note figure is about 13.8 dB over full scale.

Cause is structural, not incidental: src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:68 sets master gain to a fixed 0.7 and the piano bus to 1.0, with no voice-count normalisation and no limiter. My instrumented node census of a live note confirmed no DynamicsCompressorNode or WaveShaperNode is ever created.

Timbre is an honest but plainly synthetic approximation - three oscillators (partial ratios 1, 2.0027, 3.0142) plus a 90ms noise transient, with no sympathetic resonance, release sample or stereo image. A pianist would not mistake it for a piano recording.

Verified by instrumentation, not by reading the file. Patching AudioContext.prototype factory methods before load and playing one note produced exactly: createOscillator x3 (types sine 2, triangle 1), createBiquadFilter x1, createBufferSource x1, createBuffer x1 with {channels 1, length 4320, sampleRate 48000}. 4320/48000 = 0.090s, matching the declared lengthSeconds 0.09 in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json line 27.

decodeAudioData was called 0 times and window.fetch 0 times; the only three network requests the page made were index.html, assets/index-Q8iAhm8P.js and assets/index-DsekU4Vb.css. This corroborates the declared sampleSources: [] and 'no audio asset files ship in the artifact'.

The declaration's routing claim ('nothing bypasses the master gain') holds: exactly one node connected to AudioDestinationNode across the whole session, so my single parallel tap saw the entire output.

The declaration's surface claims check out too: declared controlCount 146 / functionalPanelControlCount 0 versus 146 elements carrying data-control-id in the DOM, all with data-functional="false"; declared keys {73, 43 white, 30 black, E1-E7} versus 43 white and 30 black measured with key ids spanning MIDI 28-100.

evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md section 6 lists twelve deviations against the reference unprompted, including that the Program OLED deliberately shows live engine status rather than an invented program name - the opposite of faking success.

Pointer: mouse-down on #key-60 measured analyser peak 0.71091 with aria-pressed="true" and data-held="true"; mouse-up returned aria-pressed="false" and peak 0.00000. Dragging from #key-60 to #key-64 with the button held transferred the note (k60 aria-pressed false, k64 true, peak 0.74700), so glissando works through the same lifecycle.
Computer keyboard: holding 'a' measured 0.54429 and released to 0.00000. A focused key also plays from the keyboard - Space on #key-60 measured 0.60415 and Enter 0.60227, both releasing to silence.

Web MIDI: injecting navigator.requestMIDIAccess with a fake port made the status strip read 'MIDI connected. (Fake MIDI Keyboard)'. 0x90 60 100 measured 0.59394; 0x80 60 0 returned 0.00000; a zero-velocity note-on (0x90 60 0) was correctly treated as note-off; CC64 held a released note at 0.35768 then dropped it to 0.00000 on CC64 0; CC123 took 0.70024 to 0.00000.

All three paths funnel through one API - noteOn(source, key, midi, velocity) in src/state/useInstrument.ts:124-133 - with per-source note ids (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:19), so pointer, keyboard and MIDI cannot steal each other's held notes.

Touch is handled independently per pointerId via the Map in src/components/Keybed.tsx:32, and pointer velocity is derived from strike depth (src/components/Keybed.tsx:18-23), which I confirmed audibly: 0.16918 at the key top vs 0.88528 at the lip.

In real Chrome without a device the status strip reported 'MIDI access was denied. (Permission to use Web MIDI API was not granted.)' and the keybed stayed fully playable - the denied path degrades honestly.

Velocity mapping is monotonic and audible in the running build: MIDI velocity 20 measured peak 0.05170 vs velocity 100 at 0.59394 (a factor of 11.5, consistent with velocityGain's 1.6-power curve plus the velocity-tracking filter in src/audio/pianoVoice.ts:50-60).

Sustain works from all three inputs. Space latched the on-screen pedal button to 'Sustain pedal (down)'; a key released under the pedal still measured 0.36168 and fell to 0.00000 on pedal-up. The MIDI CC64 path measured the same shape (0.35768 held, 0.00000 released), and the code uses a longer PEDAL_RELEASE_SECONDS 0.32 vs RELEASE_SECONDS 0.14.

All-notes-off is real on every required trigger: window blur took 0.54454 to 0.00000; a MIDI statechange (disconnect) took 0.59394 to 0.00000; CC120/CC123 took 0.70024 to 0.00000; unmount disposes the engine and closes the context (src/state/useInstrument.ts:294-306, asserted in src/state/inputs.test.tsx:290).

Voice stealing is deterministic and documented - releasing voices first, then sustained, then oldest sounding, ranked by a monotonic voiceCounter (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:259-267). I drove 40 simultaneous MIDI notes against the 32-voice cap: the build stayed stable with zero console errors and returned to peak 0.00000 afterwards.

Simplification a player would notice: the stolen voice is removed by destroy(), which calls stop(currentTime) and disconnect() with no release ramp (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:236-253), so crossing the polyphony ceiling cuts a ringing note dead rather than fading it - an audible click under a pedalled passage.

I drove every control in the running build - 146 elements carrying data-control-id, split 102 button clicks and 44 slider ArrowUp keydowns - and the master bus read peak 0.00000 / rms 0.00000 immediately afterwards. Nothing on the deck touches audio, exactly as declared.

Controls genuinely move and report: the Master Level slider went aria-valuenow 7.5 -> 8 with aria-valuetext '8.0'; 'Organ Section On' went aria-pressed false -> true; both carry data-functional="false" in the DOM.

Attribute census over the 216 interactive elements: 44 role="slider", every one of them carrying aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext (0 missing of each); 114 with aria-pressed; 0 interactive elements without an accessible name; 0 elements with a positive tabindex.

Inertness is stated in the product itself rather than hidden: the Program OLED (an aria-live="polite" region) reads 'PANEL CONTROLS: DECORATIVE', the Synth OLED reads 'SYNTH ENGINE: NOT IMPLEMENTED (PHASE 1)', and the status strip says every panel control 'moves, lights and reports its value but is otherwise inert'.
Focus is visible on keyboard traversal - tabbing through the first six controls, each matched :focus-visible and painted a 2px solid rgb(63, 169, 255) ring.

Inventory decisions were checked against the photo, not asserted: the audit drops perf.rotary.on as a printed label plus LED, and cropping the reference at the Rotary Speaker panel confirms 'ON' is a legend and an unlit LED with no button under it, while ORGAN/CLOSE MIC and STOP MODE/ANGLE are single buttons with two legends each - which is how the artifact models them.

All 11 required Phase 1 feature IDs appear in tests/feature-matrix.json, each mapped to real non-empty test files. Rebuilding from source on Node 24: pnpm test 113 passed / 9 files, typecheck clean, lint clean, build emits dist/index.html - matching inputs/verification.json.

visual.key-count measured in the browser: 43 white + 30 black = 73 keys, ids spanning MIDI 28-100 (E1-E7), all 73 boxes inside the keybed rect; black/white width ratio 0.6499 and height ratio 0.6100 against the variant spec's blackKeyHeightFraction 0.61.

visual.section-layout measured at 1440x900: deck fraction 0.5400 and keybed 0.4600 against 0.54/0.46 +/-0.025; instrument 1368.00 x 441.98 = aspect 3.0951 against the variant's measured 3.0951; width 1368/1440 = 0.9500 inside the 0.88-0.97 band; section widths as fractions of the deck measured performance 0.1400, organ 0.2000, piano 0.0850, program 0.1250, synth 0.2500, effects 0.2000 - an exact match to visual.json v1.2.0, including the corrected piano/program/synth values.

visual.control-inventory: 146 namespaced ids (perf 7, organ 24, piano 14, program 28, synth 40, effects 33), exactly two elements carrying data-oled (program and synth), and the six required section landmark groups all present on screen - nine drawbars with LED ladders and footages, model/percussion/vib switches, piano type and model selectors, program dial with eight slots, synth oscillator/filter/envelope/LFO/arp groups, and six separately outlined effect groups.

regression.chassis: at 1440x900 document.scrollHeight == innerHeight == 900 (no vertical scroll) and one continuous .chassis element wraps deck and keybed; at 390x844 the instrument renders 377.2px wide (0.967 of the viewport) with scrollWidth == 390 (no horizontal overflow) and all 73 keys still present, plus a 1x-4x zoom control for inspection.

Zero console errors or page errors were recorded across every interaction pass I ran - pointer, glissando, computer keyboard, Space/Enter, MIDI note/CC64/CC123/disconnect, 40-note stress, and driving all 146 panel controls.

issues.title: Master bus exceeds 0 dBFS from two simultaneous notes, so every chord hard-clips
issues.detail: Measured on the node feeding AudioDestinationNode with velocity-100 MIDI notes: 1 note peak 0.57581, 2 notes 1.12108, 4 notes 2.03609, 8 notes 2.81494, 16 notes 4.92725. Chrome clamps the destination to [-1, 1], so any two-note interval already distorts and a dense chord is roughly 14 dB over full scale. src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:68 sets a fixed master gain of 0.7 with no voice-count normalisation, and the node census confirms no DynamicsCompressorNode or WaveShaperNode is ever created. The suite has a test asserting a chord is louder than a single note (src/audio/pianoEngine.test.ts:183) but none asserting the sum stays under full scale.

issues.title: Stolen voices are cut without a release ramp
issues.detail: stealVoice() calls destroy() directly (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:259-267), and destroy() stops and disconnects every node at currentTime with no fade (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:236-253). Crossing the 32-voice cap therefore truncates a ringing note discontinuously, which clicks. A short 5-10ms ramp before teardown would fix it. The stealing order itself is correct and deterministic.

issues.title: Custom focus ring does not reach the outermost focusable element
issues.detail: styles.css:1388-1399 defines a 0.18em outline in var(--focus) for .knob/.fader/.drawbar/.pbtn/.pkey:focus-visible, but tabbing through the panel showed the elements that actually receive focus painting the UA default ring (2px solid rgb(63, 169, 255)) rather than the styled one - the focusable node appears to be the wrapper rather than the class the rule targets. Focus stays clearly visible, so this is cosmetic inconsistency, not an accessibility failure.

issues.title: Panel silkscreen is sub-pixel at the canonical desktop size
issues.detail: Legends are drawn at roughly 0.30% of instrument width per em, which is about 4px at the 1368px-wide desktop instrument, so the panel reads as correct micro-text density rather than legible words. The candidate declares this as deviation 1 in evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md and carries the real text in accessible names, and the artifact adds a 1x-4x zoom control below 720px width. Noted rather than penalised here because Phase 1 does not score panel fidelity, but it will matter when that axis is measured.
